---
title: "Explore multi-armed bandit policies"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

At each decision, an agent selects one of four actions, or **arms**. The reward
is a draw from that arm's stable but initially unknown distribution. From the
rewards it observes, the agent estimates each arm's mean while choosing actions
to maximize long-term total reward. In this stationary setting, the arm with the
largest mean is the best arm to choose repeatedly.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The estimate $Q_t(a)$ for an arm becomes more reliable after repeated pulls, but
only for arms the agent actually tries. Compare a purely greedy policy with
$\epsilon$-greedy and upper-confidence-bound (UCB) policies. The policy never
uses the simulation's true means when selecting an arm.
:::

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/bandit-explorer.css">
<div id="bandit-explorer" class="bandit-explorer" aria-label="Interactive multi-armed bandit policy explorer">
  <div class="bandit-toolbar clt-buttons" aria-label="Bandit simulation controls">
    <div class="bandit-policy-group" role="group" aria-label="Choose a policy">
      <span class="bandit-control-label">Policy</span>
      <button id="bandit-policy-greedy" type="button" data-policy="greedy" aria-pressed="true">Greedy</button>
      <button id="bandit-policy-epsilon" type="button" data-policy="epsilon" aria-pressed="false">ε-greedy</button>
      <button id="bandit-policy-ucb" type="button" data-policy="ucb" aria-pressed="false">UCB</button>
    </div>
    <button id="bandit-next" type="button" class="bandit-primary">Next decision</button>
    <button id="bandit-run" type="button">Run 25</button>
    <button id="bandit-run-all" type="button">Run all</button>
    <button id="bandit-reset" type="button" title="Draw a new hidden bandit and restart learning">New simulation</button>
    <output id="bandit-progress" class="bandit-progress" aria-live="polite">Decision 0</output>
  </div>

  <section class="bandit-controls" aria-label="Policy settings">
    <label class="bandit-range-control" for="bandit-epsilon">
      <span><strong>ε</strong> for ε-greedy</span>
      <input id="bandit-epsilon" type="range" min="0" max="0.5" step="0.05" value="0.20">
      <output id="bandit-epsilon-value">0.20</output>
    </label>
    <label class="bandit-range-control" for="bandit-c">
      <span><strong>c</strong> for UCB</span>
      <input id="bandit-c" type="range" min="0.25" max="3" step="0.25" value="1.00">
      <output id="bandit-c-value">1.00</output>
    </label>
    <label class="bandit-checkbox-control" for="bandit-reveal">
      <input id="bandit-reveal" type="checkbox">
      Reveal the simulation's true mean rewards
    </label>
    <label class="bandit-checkbox-control" for="bandit-optimistic">
      <input id="bandit-optimistic" type="checkbox">
      Optimistic initialization: start all <i>Q</i>(<i>a</i>) at 10
    </label>
  </section>

  <div class="bandit-workbench">
    <section class="bandit-panel bandit-plot-panel" aria-labelledby="bandit-plot-heading">
      <div class="bandit-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="bandit-plot-heading">Rewards and learning trace</h2>
        <p>Step through one 200-decision realization. Dots are sampled rewards; the dark line is the running average reward.</p>
      </div>
      <svg id="bandit-trace" viewBox="0 0 760 410" role="img" aria-label="Observed rewards and running average over decisions"></svg>
      <div class="bandit-legend">
        <span><i class="bandit-observation-key"></i>Observed reward</span>
        <span><i class="bandit-average-key"></i>Running average</span>
        <span id="bandit-reference-legend" hidden><i class="bandit-reference-key"></i>Best arm mean</span>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>

  <section class="bandit-panel bandit-details" aria-labelledby="bandit-details-heading">
      <div class="bandit-panel-heading"><h2 id="bandit-details-heading">Current decision</h2></div>
      <div class="bandit-decision-summary">
      <div id="bandit-action" class="bandit-action" aria-live="polite">Choose a policy, then make the first decision.</div>
      <p id="bandit-explanation" class="bandit-explanation">All estimates start at zero because the agent has not observed any rewards yet.</p>
      <div class="bandit-metrics">
        <div><span>Last reward</span><strong id="bandit-last-reward">—</strong></div>
        <div><span>Running average</span><strong id="bandit-running-average">—</strong></div>
        <div><span>Most pulled arm</span><strong id="bandit-most-pulled">—</strong></div>
      </div>
      </div>
      <div class="bandit-knowledge">
      <h3>What the agent knows</h3>
      <div id="bandit-arm-table" class="bandit-arm-table" aria-live="polite"></div>
      <p class="bandit-note"><em>Q<sub>t</sub>(a)</em> is the sample-average reward for arm <em>a</em>. UCB adds an uncertainty bonus that shrinks as an arm is pulled more often.</p>
      </div>
  </section>

  <details class="bandit-answer">
    <summary>Reveal the simulation's reward distributions</summary>
    <p>Each arm has a fixed Normal reward distribution. Its mean is the arm's correct long-run expected reward, which the policies try to estimate from sampled rewards.</p>
    <div id="bandit-answer-table" class="bandit-answer-table"></div>
  </details>

</div>
```
